summary: OpenSplat is a free C++ implementation of three-dimensional Gaussian splat training, licensed under the GNU Affero General Public Licence version 3, now developed inside the WebODM drone-mapping ecosystem. It is the plainest tool in this group: a command that takes a reconstruction someone else solved, in ODX, OpenSfM, COLMAP, OpenMVG or Nerfstudio project form, and trains a splat from it on an NVIDIA, AMD or Apple graphics card, or on the processor alone at roughly a hundredth of the speed. Two things make it matter to a standards group. First, it writes four different splat containers from one training run — plain PLY, the compact .splat, Niantic's SPZ and Spark's .RAD level-of-detail format — which makes it a useful witness to how unsettled that layer is, and its .RAD writer is a port of another project's Rust tool rather than an implementation of a published specification. Second, it is the only tool scored here that carries a real coordinate reference system through training: because its inputs come from mapping pipelines, it keeps the input translation and scale by default and offers a switch to centre the result for viewers that cannot cope. What it does not do is run on a phone, solve its own camera poses, produce a mesh, or write a single field about licence, authorship or units into any of its four outputs.

coverage.note: OpenSplat carries its own splat rasteriser three times over — a CUDA path, a HIP path for AMD and a Metal path for Apple, with a processor-only fallback — so the projection, sorting and blending are all its own. There is no render graph and no pass structure, because a training run draws one thing.

coverage.note: OpenSplat is a command-line trainer that turns a finished reconstruction into a splat file, so it keeps no places and has nothing to export beyond that file.

sources.title: OpenSplat README
sources.quote: A free and open source implementation of 3D [gaussian splatting](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HVv_IQKlafQ) written in C++, focused on being portable, lean and fast.

coverage.note: OpenSplat is a command-line trainer for Gaussian splats; it does not recognise a known object from its model or report its pose.

sources.title: OpenSplat README (commit 688944f)
sources.quote: A free and open source implementation of 3D [gaussian splatting](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HVv_IQKlafQ) written in C++, focused on being portable, lean and fast.

coverage.note: OpenSplat trains from camera poses that arrive as per-image placements in a reconstruction project, with no time or sequence kept. Time-associated pose series are outside a splat trainer.

sources.title: OpenSplat README (commit 688944f)
sources.quote: A free and open source implementation of 3D [gaussian splatting](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HVv_IQKlafQ) written in C++, focused on being portable, lean and fast.

coverage.note: OpenSplat writes PLY, .splat, SPZ and .RAD files whose extension rules belong to those formats, and it defines no container or extension scheme of its own.
